- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if 2+ consecutive days show negative sentiment.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive price drops or sentiment dips), reduce forecast slope toward historical mean.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.67 to -0.67), model should not overcorrect — cap forecast adjustments to ±10% of recent 7-day average to avoid volatility overfitting.
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5 days of horizon, reduce subsequent forecast by 2–3% per day to account for lagged market correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, assume sentiment is misaligned — reduce forecast by 3–5% to reflect sentiment-price mismatch.
